extra.message: User-supplied data from request.form['data_obj'] is hex-decoded, written to a file, then loaded via pickle.load(). Deserializing attacker-controlled pickle data leads to arbitrary code execution (RCE), as pickle can invoke arbitrary callables via __reduce__.

The 'input' value from the URL route is base64-decoded and passed to yaml.load() without a SafeLoader. yaml.load() with the default loader can instantiate arbitrary Python objects (e.g. via !!python/object/apply tags), allowing remote code execution from attacker-controlled YAML.

User-supplied XML from request.form['customers'] is parsed with xml.dom.pulldom.parseString, which uses the default expat parser without disabling external entity / DTD processing. This permits XML External Entity (XXE) attacks to read local files (e.g. file:///etc/passwd) or perform SSRF, and the expanded node content is reflected back to the page.

extra.message: Authentication is performed against hardcoded credentials (username == 'admin' and password == 'admin') embedded directly in the source code. Hardcoded credentials cannot be rotated and are trivially guessable, allowing authentication bypass.

The /confidential endpoint's only access check is `if(session['loggedin'])`, which merely tests for presence of a session key (any truthy value). The /webmaster route (Webmaster.py:12) sets session['loggedin'] to a random UUID for any unauthenticated visitor, so an attacker can obtain a valid 'loggedin' session by simply visiting /webmaster and then access confidential data. This is broken access control / missing proper authorization.

The Flask SECRET_KEY is hardcoded to the weak, predictable value 'random'. The secret key is used to sign session cookies; a known/guessable key allows attackers to forge session cookies (e.g. set session['loggedin']) and bypass authentication.

Flask debug mode is enabled (app.debug = True). In debug mode an unhandled exception exposes the interactive Werkzeug debugger, which permits arbitrary Python code execution via the console, as well as leaking source code and environment details. This must never be enabled in production.
The application binds to 0.0.0.0, exposing the (debug-enabled) development server on all network interfaces. Combined with debug mode this dramatically increases remote attack surface.

The /webmaster page exposes plaintext usernames, passwords and secret ids. The route (Webmaster.py) has no authentication at all and is reachable by any anonymous user, disclosing sensitive credentials.
